observations.seen: Munich night frames have reasonable flood key on turf, but the stands are flat dark with unlit capsule crowd. Frames 3 and 4 are flat ambient: the sepia frame is a single warm wash, and the grey frame is washed-out low-contrast concrete.
Players use soft blob ellipses plus faint directional shadows in frames 3 and 4. Goal net and posts cast almost no grounded shadow, and there is no contact darkening at the feet.
No visible environment reflection. Ball, turf and floor all read diffuse, and the grey court has no sheen despite looking like a polished indoor floor.
Stadium tiers hold pill-shaped crowd tokens and a truss light tower. Frames 3 and 4 have a mostly empty backdrop with a blocky wall and stand-in billboard frame.
No indoor haze, no light shafts from the floods and no depth fog. The grey frame looks foggy, but it reads as low contrast rather than as authored haze.
Turf has a noisy grass texture with a motion-blur-like smear. The goal net is a solid white translucent slab with no mesh detail. Kits are flat colour.
Low-poly stylized players with decent proportions and readable kits. The goal net is overly opaque and the crowd is primitive capsules.
Kickoff frames are well centred but subjects are tiny, about 10% of the frame, with a large empty floor. Gameplay frames frame the attack and goal well.
Uses a perspective broadcast angle rather than orthographic. The gameplay camera tracks the ball sensibly, but the kickoff frames are high and distant.
No bloom on floodlights, no tonemapped punch and no vignette. The sepia frame is a heavy colour grade that muddies everything.
Running poses look dynamic, and the keeper is shown diving in frame 2. Kickoff players stand in stiff T-like idle poses.
Clean scorebar, timer, possession bar and controls strip with consistent styling. The possession bar has no team colour split, and the kickoff frames show no HUD.
